briefing.text: Information Technology still leads all three platforms on 4 Nov: News buzz 87.7 (mentions +11%, sentiment 0.10; NVDA, MSFT, AMD), X buzz 94.2 (mentions +21%) and Reddit buzz 92.6 (mentions -9%; AMD, MU, NVDA). Utilities is the clearest riser on social: Reddit buzz +5.0 (+8.3 over the week, mentions +239%) and X buzz +3.4 (+5.7 over the week, mentions +213%), driven by VST, CEG and NEE. On News, Consumer Staples (+1.3, WMT, KHC, KO), Health Care (+1.2, CVS, AMGN, NVO) and Communication Services (+1.1, mentions +29%) gained. Financials fell most on News (buzz -3.4, -4.5 over the week; BAC, UBS, MS) and Financial Services on Reddit (-8.5, -19.4 over the week); Energy also eased on News (-1.5, mentions -12%) and Materials on Reddit (-3.2, mentions -33%).

FIG #1: RBC cut its target to $24 from $28 (sector perform) and a headline notes shares fell despite a strong Q3; the news is negative, so it fits the 17% one-day drop rather than a positive catalyst.
MELI #2: Scotiabank cut its target to $2,300 from $2,800 (sector outperform); 22 of 54 articles are negative, which fits the 13% drop that is a 5.1-sigma move.
DDOG #3: TD Cowen and Rosenblatt both lowered targets (to $275 and $285, both rated buy); 47 of 89 articles are negative, matching the 7% fall and 26% drop over five days.
FSLR #4: News is mostly positive (47 of 55 articles) but the headlines are solar-sector watchlists and a post-quarter review, so it explains attention more than a single event.
RACE #5: Ferrari reported EPS of $2.76 on Tuesday, beating consensus, and shares rose 4.3% on 4 Nov; the news explains the ranking.
NDX #6: Headlines point to a broad tech selloff (Reddit down 8%); the index fell 6.4% in a day, so the news explains the move.
NEE #7: Headlines are routine (share price above the 200-day average, utility stocks as a hedge); they do not explain the rank, which comes from social attention and a Kalshi market on a Dominion takeover.
MCD #11: Headlines cover a Wall Street warning after the stock rally and plans for new value menus; this fits the high attention.

FIG ranks first (score 0.93) because trading volume is 2.0x normal, attention on Reddit and X is about 1.4x normal, and the 24h price move of -16.9% is a 4.5-sigma event; its Kalshi market on customers above $100k ARR resolves soon. MELI is second (0.92) on a 5.1-sigma price drop of 12.6%, volume 1.5x normal and attention on X 1.1x normal, with Kalshi markets on items sold carrying the most volume. DDOG is third (0.87) and has the highest attention reading of the three (1.7x normal overall, 1.6x on X, 280 X mentions) with volume 1.1x normal; its price move is only 1.3 sigma, so attention rather than price is the main driver. All three moved up sharply from the previous pull (FIG from 326, DDOG from 111).

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
